items.imageCaption: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP | Ronen Zvulun/Reuters
items.author: Tal Shalev, Oren Liebermann
items.excerpt: The wheels of Israel’s political machine are turning. But that doesn’t mean they’re going anywhere soon. In the latest elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lost the parliamentary majority that kept him in power over the past four years. But his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, still faces a difficult task in unseating Israel’s longest-serving leader after being tasked with forming the next government. On paper, Eisenkot has a clear majority, with 67 of 120 seats in Israel’s legislature, the Knesset. But those seats come from six ideologically diverse parties, from right-wing to Arab parties.
